race_context: The Tri-Creek School Corporation is based in Lowell in southern Lake County and serves West Creek, Cedar Creek and Eagle Creek townships {tc_news_2023}{tc_districts}. It enrolled about 2,800 students in 2024–25 at Lowell High School, Lowell Middle School and three elementary schools (Oak Hill, Three Creeks and Lake Prairie), according to federal data {plainschools_tc}. Dr. Andy Anderson is superintendent {tc_superintendent}.

The board has five members: three elected from electoral districts (District 1, West Creek Township; District 2, Cedar Creek Township; District 3, Eagle Creek Township) and two elected at large {tc_districts}{lc_directory}{lc_results_2022}. The board redrew the three districts' precinct lines in March 2025; District 2 now takes in Cedar Creek Township precincts 2, 5, 6 and 7 and Cedar Lake Township precincts 8 and 9 {tc_districts}. District races appear only on the ballots of voters in that district; the at-large race appears on every ballot in the corporation {lc_sample_cct01}{lc_sample_cct02}.

At-large seats (2026): the ballot says 'Vote for not more than Two (2),' not one as on the state list {lc_sample_cct01}. Both at-large seats were last filled in 2022, when Robert Hayden and Nathan Kleefisch won {lc_results_2022}. Their terms end Dec. 31, 2026 {tc_board}. Hayden is running again. Kleefisch is not on the county candidate list {lc_candidates}. The only candidates are Hayden and Cody Van Deursen, so with two candidates for two seats, both are effectively unopposed {lc_sample_cct01}{lc_candidates}.

District 2 seat (2026): Katie Kimbrell won the seat (then listed as Cedar Creek) in 2022 and resigned from the board on April 8, 2026 {lc_results_2022}{tc_vandeursen}. The board appointed Cody Van Deursen to finish her term, which runs April 30–Dec. 31, 2026 {tc_vandeursen}. Van Deursen is running at large instead, so Craig Rosinski is the only District 2 candidate ('Vote For One (1) Only') {lc_candidates}{lc_sample_cct02}. The board will therefore have at least one new member in January 2027.

Not on this ballot: board President Andy Laub (District 1, elected 2024, term through 2028) and Amber Miller (District 3). The board appointed Miller to finish the term of Kyle Mitsch, who resigned April 19, 2026; that term runs through Dec. 31, 2028 {tc_board}{tc_miller}{lc_results_2024}.

Operating referendum on the same ballot (2026): the board asks voters to approve a property tax rate of up to $0.1738 per $100 of assessed value, raising no more than $3 million a year for eight years. The money would replace lost property tax revenue and pay for bus transportation, student programs and school safety. The ballot says the bill on a $300,000 median home would rise $245 a year {lc_sample_cct01}{dlgf_tc_det}. The state Department of Local Government Finance approved the ballot language June 22, 2026 {dlgf_tc_det}. The district's June 23, 2026 spending plan estimates about $1.04 million a year for buses, $1.54 million for student programs and $419,000 for safety {dlgf_tc_plan}.

Budget and SEA 1 (2025–2026): the district says Senate Enrolled Act 1, together with tax-increment financing (TIF) districts in Lowell, will cost it $2 million to more than $2.6 million a year in property tax revenue from 2026 to 2031 {tc_referendum}. It says it has cut more than 30 positions and reduced department budgets over the past three years {tc_referendum}. It also says that if the referendum fails, major changes such as dismantling the bus system 'would have to be seriously considered' and student programs would face 'phased elimination' over three years {tc_referendum}. These are the district's own statements on its referendum information page.

2023 referendum: voters rejected an earlier Tri-Creek operating referendum in the May 2, 2023 primary {ipm_2023}{dlgf_tc_det}. That measure would have funded staff pay, expanded programs and preschool. The district now describes it as an 'expansion' request and the 2026 measure as a 'stability' request {tc_referendum}{tc_news_2023}.

Forums and differences: no candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the 2026 Tri-Creek board races was found, and no candidate's position on the referendum was found. Because every race is effectively uncontested, there are no head-to-head contrasts to report.

candidates.summary: Current board member, appointed in April 2026 to finish the District 2 term of Katie Kimbrell; now running for an at-large seat {tc_vandeursen}{lc_candidates}.
background: Owner and operator of Van Deursen Farms, Inc. {tc_vandeursen}
Born and raised in Lowell. He graduated from Lowell High School in 2002 and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of St. Francis in 2006 {tc_vandeursen}.
Parent of students in the district {tc_vandeursen}.
path_to_ballot: Filed June 10, 2026 for Tri-Creek School Board, At Large, with no party listed; the state list shows him as Nonpartisan {lc_candidates}{in_list}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member (appointed April 30, 2026) {tc_vandeursen}.

Asked on his district biography why Tri-Creek and public education matter to him, he wrote: 'I was born and raised here, and my children have attended and continue to attend Tri-Creek Schools.' {tc_vandeursen}
gaps: No campaign statements, website, questionnaire responses, news coverage, endorsements or finance reports found.
How he voted on the 2026 referendum resolutions, and his position on the referendum, not found (board minutes are on BoardDocs, which could not be read).
Why he is running at large rather than for the District 2 seat he was appointed to not found.
Whether the at-large seats carry a residency requirement (the 2026 county directory labels them 'At Large - District 3' and 'At Large - District 1') not confirmed.

candidates.summary: Incumbent. Board vice president, first elected at large in 2022 {tc_hayden}{lc_results_2022}.
background: Parent of students in the district {tc_hayden}.
path_to_ballot: Filed June 16, 2026 for Tri-Creek School Board, At Large, with no party listed; the state list shows him as Nonpartisan {lc_candidates}{in_list}.
Won an at-large seat in 2022 with about 40% of the vote in a three-way race for two seats (3,257 votes), placing first {lc_results_2022}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member and serves as board vice president {tc_hayden}{tc_board}.

On his district biography he wrote that he wants 'all children in the Tri-Creek School Corporation to receive the best education that the teachers, staff, and board can give them' and to remember Tri-Creek 'as a school district that guided them and gave them all it could toward a future successful career.' {tc_hayden}
gaps: No campaign statements, website, questionnaire responses, news coverage, endorsements or finance reports found.
His votes on the 2026 referendum resolutions and on budget cuts, and his public position on the referendum, not found (BoardDocs minutes could not be read).
